text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Municipalities to pay more: Ontario to shift cost burden for welfare, child care, public health, care of elderly.
- Trade mission skirts rights ills: South Koreans decry labour laws.
- Junior hockey players travel isolated, tough road: The sport's culture is macho, but far from home, young players can be vulnerable.
- Talks clear way for Hebron deal: Israel, PLO agree on withdrawl dates.
- Woman's suit goes to top U.S. court: Clinton seeks temporary immunity.
- Convicted killer on verge of full parole: Less than four years ago, David Mattison was sent to jail for the fatal shooting of his wife. If all goes well for him, he may soon be out.
- Exporters fear surging dollar: Firms competing against foreign goods say they'll be hurt if Canada's currency rises too high.
- Furniture firms sitting pretty: Times are good for Canadian trend-setters.
- Branson flies high on felled balloon: Failed flight still yields Virgin PR.
- Oil and gas burn brightly for market analysts.
- Retirees facing massive 'tax grab': Study blasts Paul Martin's planned Seniors Benefit program.
- Suharto favorite seen making move on Bre-X.
- Shareholder wins landmark ruling on bank circulars.
